title: A Drone Strike on Iraq's Khor Mor Field Cuts 70% of Kurdish Power, China's Producer Inflation Hits 5.7%, and Egypt Reopens Its Tripoli Embassy After 12 Years
subhead: An unmanned aerial strike forced a production halt at northern Iraq's Khor Mor gas facility and knocked out electricity across more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region, even as oil futures eased after President Trump said fresh US strikes on Iran were unlikely. Elsewhere, China's October producer price index jumped 5.7 percent to a four-year high on rising energy input costs while consumer inflation cooled, Cairo reopened its embassy in Tripoli after a 12-year closure, and G7 foreign ministers convened in Paris to press Washington on Ukraine and Iran.

sections.heading: Drone Strike Halts Iraq's Khor Mor Gas Field as Trump Calls Fresh Iran Strikes 'Unlikely'
sections.body:
An explosive drone struck the Khor Mor gas facility in Iraq's Sulaymaniyah province late Sunday, halting gas production and triggering widespread blackouts that left more than 70 percent of northern Iraq's Kurdish region without electricity (Al Jazeera, Star, Yeni Şafak). The strike coincided with the rollout of US Central Command's new 'Iron Gate' task force, established over the weekend to interdict Iranian overland supply routes across the region (Al Jazeera, Yeni Şafak).

In Washington, President Donald Trump signaled a potential pause in direct military strikes on Iranian territory while defending the eight-month campaign. Crude oil futures fell at Monday's Asian open after Trump stated that fresh US attacks on Iran were 'unlikely' and said Tehran remained interested in a diplomatic settlement, even while describing the military campaign to date as 'one of the best things we have ever done' (Reuters, Wall Street Journal, Anadolu Agency, TRT Haber). Secretary of State Marco Rubio added that while the Iran war was 'not necessarily popular,' it was required to stop a nuclear threat, accusing Iranian negotiators of making 'outrageous and ridiculous' demands (AP News, Times of Israel).

In Yemen, the internationally recognized government's armed forces reported conducting 992 operations across multiple provinces that killed or wounded 267 Houthi fighters at a loss of nine government officers, while Houthi authorities in Sanaa said the death toll from Saudi coalition airstrikes on the capital rose to 44 dead and 40 injured (Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: Even as the White House cools talk of new direct strikes on Iran after midterm losses, the Khor Mor blackout shows militia drone attacks on Iraqi energy infrastructure remain an active pressure point outside formal US-Iran talks.

sections.heading: Post-Midterm Reckoning in Washington as G7 Ministers Meet in Paris
sections.body:
Reflecting on Tuesday's Republican midterm defeat in a Sunday interview with CBS's '60 Minutes,' President Donald Trump acknowledged that his administration's deportation policies had been 'too tough' and hurt Republicans at the ballot box, stating he wants to work out a bipartisan immigration agreement with Democrats (NBC News). Separately, Trump cited voter fatigue with the Iran war and what he described as 'great dislike' for Israel among segments of the electorate as factors in the midterm losses, while stating that incoming Israeli coalition formateur Gadi Eisenkot and outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu are 'very similar in terms of their policy' (Anadolu Agency, Times of Israel). Trump also floated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin next week (TRT Haber).

Inside the White House, the departure of Chief of Staff Susie Wiles deprived corporate leaders of a key business-friendly interlocutor, while reports that senior adviser Stephen Miller would take over the role drew criticism from lawmakers in both parties (Wall Street Journal, Yeni Şafak). Meanwhile, a scheduled US deportation flight carrying Iranian nationals was scuttled at the last minute following legal intervention, according to an attorney for the detainees (AP News).

Across the Atlantic, G7 foreign ministers gathered in Paris on Monday, where European governments plan to press Washington on securing long-term support for Ukraine and avoiding further military escalation with Iran (France 24).
sections.whyItMatters: Trump's public admission on '60 Minutes' that immigration enforcement and the Iran war cost Republicans Congress signals a tactical pivot toward deal-making ahead of January's power transfer on Capitol Hill.

sections.heading: China's Producer Inflation Surges 5.7% to Four-Year High While Consumer Demand Cools
sections.body:
China's National Bureau of Statistics reported on Monday that the country's producer price index (PPI) rose 5.7 percent year-on-year in October — the highest reading in more than four years and above the 5.3 percent forecast in a Reuters poll — driven by elevated global energy and raw material costs (CNBC, Bloomberg, Financial Times). At the same time, China's consumer price index (CPI) edged lower in October as domestic household spending and property-sector demand remained sluggish (Financial Times, CNBC).

Asian equity markets steadied on Monday morning following last week's sharp technology sell-off, which UBS chief executive Sergio Ermotti noted had occurred because AI investors were 'pricing for perfection' (CNA). In Australia, the housing downturn deepened ahead of another expected interest rate hike by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) (Wall Street Journal).
sections.whyItMatters: A 5.7 percent factory-gate inflation print paired with soft consumer prices squeezes Chinese industrial profit margins: manufacturers are paying war-inflated energy costs without being able to pass them on to domestic shoppers.

sections.heading: Egypt Reopens Tripoli Embassy After 12 Years as Gaza Landslide Kills Five
sections.body:
Egypt formally reopened its embassy in Tripoli, Libya, over the weekend, restoring diplomatic representation in the Libyan capital for the first time since violence forced the mission's closure in 2014 (Yeni Şafak). Meanwhile, inside Egypt, a passenger train derailment in the Ayat district of Giza province killed at least seven people and injured 112 others (Habertürk).

In the Levant, torrential winter rains triggered a collapse of sand and rock onto displaced Palestinians' tents in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, killing five people — including three children and one woman (Habertürk, TRT Haber). In the occupied West Bank, Israeli troops shot and wounded a 13-year-old Palestinian boy in the chest during a raid in Jenin, while in Israel, ultra-Orthodox Shas party leader Aryeh Deri announced he will step down from his Knesset seat before parliament convenes after his party's tally fell from 11 seats to 6 in the October 27 election (Anadolu Agency, Star). In Europe, tens of thousands of protesters dressed in red marched through Amsterdam demanding Dutch sanctions on Israel, as Dutch Foreign Minister Berendsen reaffirmed commitments toward a Palestinian state (Euronews, TRT Haber).
sections.whyItMatters: Cairo's return to Tripoli after 12 years of backing rival eastern Libyan factions marks a major diplomatic realignment in North Africa, giving Egypt direct leverage in the UN-recognized capital alongside Turkey.

sections.heading: Antalya Hosts 196 Nations for COP31 as Pope Leo XIV Rebukes Milei's Austerity in Argentina
sections.body:
Delegations from 196 countries convened in Antalya, Turkey, on Monday for the opening of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), the first time Turkey has hosted the flagship global climate summit (Anadolu Agency, Yeni Şafak). Speaking ahead of the opening plenary, Singapore's environment minister said COP31 is unlikely to produce brand-new emissions targets, arguing negotiators already have 'enough to work on' implementing existing pledges amid a global climate adaptation financing gap where developing nations receive less than $32 billion against an estimated $305 billion annual need (SCMP, Ekonomim).

In South America, Pope Leo XIV delivered a sharp public critique of Argentine President Javier Milei's austerity program during the second stop of his 12-day Latin American tour in Buenos Aires, urging the government to protect democracy and ensure economic growth benefits the poor (The Guardian, DW). Meanwhile, in New Zealand, centrist party figure Qiulae Wong — whose party is positioned as a potential kingmaker after Saturday's deadlocked election — told reporters on Monday that populist politics are failing voters worldwide and called for pragmatic coalition building (CNA).
sections.whyItMatters: As COP31 opens in Antalya, the gap between $305 billion in needed adaptation funds and under $32 billion in actual disbursements makes climate finance — rather than new emissions targets — the summit's central fault line.

bottomLine: Monday opened with conflicting signals across the Middle East energy and security landscape: oil prices dipped after President Trump said fresh US strikes on Iran were 'unlikely,' yet an overnight drone attack halted northern Iraq's Khor Mor gas field and cut electricity to more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region as CENTCOM activated its 'Iron Gate' land-interdiction task force. In Washington, Trump acknowledged on '60 Minutes' that tough deportations and the Iran war hurt Republicans in the midterms, offering Democrats an immigration deal as G7 foreign ministers met in Paris. Meanwhile, China's producer inflation jumped 5.7 percent to a four-year high on energy costs, Egypt reopened its embassy in Tripoli after 12 years, and 196 countries opened the COP31 climate summit in Antalya.
sources: Reuters, AP News, Al Jazeera, CNBC, Financial Times, Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, The Guardian, NBC News, CBS News, DW, France 24, CNA, SCMP, Times of Israel, Euronews, Anadolu Agency, TRT Haber, Habertürk, Ekonomim, Yeni Şafak, Star
